headline: Models predict single-cell perturbation responses from population and trajectory data
label: Single Cell Perturbation Response Modeling
summary: Preprints and 2026 publications pair perturbation prediction with population-level joint modeling, trajectory inference, and cross-context evaluation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned prediction of single-cell perturbation responses by transferring information across contexts and datasets. PopPert fits a low-rank Gaussian copula to joint expression distributions from unpaired single-cell data to predict responses at the population level. AnnFlux learns object-conditioned neural SDE drift fields in latent cell-state space to model perturbation trajectories and predict unseen perturbations. scDRP pairs a disentangled beta-VAE with conditional optimal transport to estimate individual treatment effects, while State is trained on expression across diverse contexts with Cell-Eval for evaluation. What is new is population-level joint modeling from unpaired data alongside explicit cross-context evaluation. SUDO and DRIFT address adjacent axes: unbalanced dynamic optimal transport with general convex growth penalties, and division-resolved flow inference in proliferating populations.
